quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: You should signal continuously while turning because it:

options.text: Is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, cyclists, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:

options.text: The same as a yield sign.
The light is about to turn green.
The same as a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Yield to other traffic and pedestrians. Go only when it is safe. This is the same as a stop sign.

questions.question: At intersections with a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic or merging vehicles that are close enough to cause a collision.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be alert. Proceed carefully after checking for other traffic.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Park with all four wheels off the highway if possible.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park with all four wheels off the highway if possible.
questions.explanation: Move your disabled vehicle off the main highway if you can. Park with all four wheels off the road.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders have the right to:

options.text: Use a full traffic lane.
Use half of a traffic lane.
Use the shoulder of a road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a full traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists have the right to use a complete lane. Two motorcyclists may share a lane if they choose. Never pass a motorcycle within the same lane.

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when safe.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up and smoothly merge with fast traffic on the interstate. Do not stop before entering.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking traffic.
Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before turning. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a collision.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when needed to avoid a collision. Do not use it just because a driver or cyclist is moving slowly or blocking your way.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, what should you do?

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop completely behind the gates. Wait until the gates lift and the tracks are clear, then go.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely behind the gates. Wait until the gates lift and the tracks are clear, then go.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when warning signs, lights, or flaggers are present. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: What are "no zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear in blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or steer safely.
Areas where cars have enough space to travel behind the truck.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear in blind spots or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or steer safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas where cars cannot be seen by truck drivers or are positioned too close. This greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: Which factor affects how quickly a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects alcohol absorption. Other factors include biological sex and how much food is in the stomach. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

questions.question: Even small amounts of alcohol can affect a driver's:

options.text: Right-of-way privileges.
Judgment and physical coordination.
Knowledge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and physical coordination.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can harm judgment and coordination, even below the legal limit. Driving impaired, even with small amounts of alcohol, can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: Alcohol is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and harms concentration and alertness.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge right.
Divided highway begins.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lane ends.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane is ending ahead. Drivers in that lane must merge.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Do both A and B.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both A and B.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for another train on any track. Do not go until all gates are lifted and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: At an intersection with four stop signs, give the right-of-way to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived before you.
Is across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived before you.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrived. If vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right goes first.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
Prevents the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on ice and snow can lock the front wheels and cause loss of steering. Reduce speed to avoid needing hard braking in these conditions.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signal:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
Both when pulling up to and when leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when pulling up to and when leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal when pulling up to a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Stop ahead.
There is roadwork or maintenance ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork or maintenance ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about construction, maintenance, and utility work areas. These signs help you drive safely through dangerous zones. Fines may double in areas marked by these signs.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to turn than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop. A passenger vehicle at 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther back than you would follow a passenger vehicle.
One car length back so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would follow a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the truck driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Tailgating removes your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: A vehicle ahead has its high beam headlights on at night. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your headlights once quickly.
Keep your high beams on.
Look toward the oncoming vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your headlights once quickly.
questions.explanation: Flash your headlights once to signal the other driver to dim their lights. If they do not dim them, look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded. Do not retaliate with your own high beams.

questions.question: What should you do to pass on a two-lane road?

options.text: Use your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is difficult to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. They may seem slower than they really are. Only pass when you are sure you can safely change lanes. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle has passed and there is enough space.
